sources.verdict: VALIDATION ONLY, not discovery. The web service requires session cookies + a hidden csrfToken, accepts only a 9/12-digit VRN (optional GB prefix) and 303-redirects to /known (returns registered name + address) or /unknown. Company names and CRNs are rejected with a form error. Under load the /known result page returns HTTP 429 (no Retry-After) while the 303 verdict still comes back, so validity survives throttling but the name needed for matching does not. REST API v1 is retired (404) and v2 requires OAuth application credentials (401). VIES no longer covers GB (INVALID_INPUT); XI works only for Northern-Ireland-registered traders.

sources.verdict: DEAD END for VAT as a structured identifier. Supplier parties carry Companies House (GB-COH) or supplier-registration (GB-SRS) ids; no VAT identifier scheme exists in award releases. GB-format VAT numbers do appear incidentally in free-text fields (1 payload(s), e.g. a supplier list), unlinked to any party id, so they cannot be attributed to a company without the same verify+match step.

tests.note: CRNs (Companies House) and VRNs (HMRC) come from independent issuing sequences. Any rank correlation between them reflects issue date (older firms have both lower CRNs and older VRNs), not derivability; no deterministic rule maps one to the other.

sources.verdict: UK VRNs are NOT derivable from CRNs (independent number spaces, no equality, Mod-97 does not link them). France contrast: FR VAT = key(SIREN) is computable and VIES confirms it. GB EORIs are derived FROM the VRN (GB+VRN+000), so the EORI API can corroborate a VRN but cannot discover one; there is no EORI-by-name search. Charity Commission and FCA APIs require keys, the FCA register is a JS app and the ICO register is behind a Cloudflare challenge; none publish VAT numbers.

sources.source: Open web discovery (search engines, Clearbit autocomplete, domain guessing) + site crawl
sources.verdict: The ONLY source in this study that yields VAT numbers for a company not already identified by VRN. Bottleneck is domain discovery: scripted search is blocked (captcha / JS challenge / 429 / 500) or silently degraded (Bing returns HTTP 200 with irrelevant, IP-localised results), so production needs a licensed search API or a pre-built company->domain index. Free entity-linked source: Wikidata P2622 (Companies House ID) -> P856 (website), large companies only. Crawl targets: footer, /terms, /legal, /privacy, /contact, /about.

hmrc_result_page_throttle_2026-11-17.how: after three full pipeline runs (~60 HMRC lookups in ~40 min from one IP), probed one known-valid VRN once per minute with fresh sessions
hmrc_result_page_throttle_2026-11-17.observed: POST always 303 -> /known; GET /known returned 429 from 12:31:14 to 12:40:18 (10 probes) and 200 at 12:41:19 -> throttle window ~10 min, no Retry-After header
hmrc_result_page_throttle_2026-11-17.implication: budget lookups (<= ~1 per 3 s, cache by VRN) and treat the 303 Location as the validity verdict; name retrieval needs back-off or an authenticated API v2 client

hmrc_throttle_in_pipeline_runs_2026-11-1.note: recorded from pipeline runs whose raw hmrc_http_log.json was later overwritten; the final run served all 17 verdicts from data/hmrc_cache.json and made 0 HMRC requests

run_1_~13:20_utc.resume_10min_rounds: 12 attempts: 9x429 then 3x200; first name after 7 consecutive 429 rounds (~70 min)

development_observations.search_engines: Bing served IP-localised junk (Romanian/Chinese sites) for most scripted queries; Mojeek captcha, Startpage JS challenge, Brave 429, Yahoo 500, DuckDuckGo 202 anomaly page

conclusion: No UK public registry, procurement or gazette source maps company -> VAT number. HMRC (and the EORI API) only validate a VRN you already have. The viable discovery path is company website -> VAT text in footer/legal pages -> Mod-97/9755 -> HMRC validation -> entity match against the Companies House name/postcode.
